title: Configure credentials
description: Set up AWS CLI credentials, default region, and output format — run once after installing awscli to authenticate all subsequent commands.

breakdown.meaning: AWS CLI entry point
Interactively set access key, secret key, region, and output format

flags.description: Store credentials under a named profile instead of the default
Show current configuration values without changing them
Set a single config value non-interactively (e.g. aws configure set region us-east-1)
Print all configured profile names

output:
AWS Access Key ID [None]: AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE
AWS Secret Access Key [None]: ****
Default region name [None]: us-east-1
Default output format [None]: json
tip: Use named profiles (--profile prod) rather than overwriting the default to manage multiple accounts safely. In EC2, ECS, or Lambda, prefer IAM roles over static access keys — the SDK picks them up automatically without any configuration.

title: Check current identity
description: Return the AWS account ID, ARN, and user ID for the currently active credentials — the fastest way to verify which account and identity is in use.

breakdown.meaning: AWS Security Token Service — manages temporary credentials and identity
Return the account ID, user ID, and ARN for the current credentials

flags.description: Use a specific named profile
Plain text output for shell scripting
Extract just the account ID field using JMESPath

tip: Run this before any destructive operation to confirm you are acting in the correct account and region. Combine with --query 'Account' --output text to extract just the account ID for use in shell scripts or CI validation checks.

title: List and switch profiles
description: List all configured AWS CLI profiles — use --profile on any command or set AWS_PROFILE to switch between accounts and roles without reconfiguring.

breakdown.meaning: AWS CLI configuration management
Print the names of all profiles in ~/.aws/config and ~/.aws/credentials

flags.description: Use the named profile for a single command
Environment variable to set the active profile for an entire shell session

tip: Set AWS_PROFILE as a shell environment variable to apply a profile for the whole session without repeating --profile on every command. Add 'role_arn' and 'source_profile' to a profile in ~/.aws/config to automatically assume a role when that profile is used.

title: List S3 buckets and objects
description: List S3 buckets or the contents of a bucket — use --recursive to traverse all prefixes, --human-readable for legible file sizes.

breakdown.meaning: List S3 buckets or objects in a bucket
Target bucket (omit to list all buckets)
List all objects under all prefixes, not just the top level
Display sizes in KB, MB, GB instead of raw bytes

flags.description: List all objects in all subdirectories (prefixes)
Show sizes as KB/MB/GB
Show total object count and size at the end
Number of objects per API page — reduce if hitting timeout errors on large buckets

tip: Omit the bucket argument to list all buckets: 'aws s3 ls'. Use --page-size to avoid timeout errors on very large buckets. For programmatic use, prefer 'aws s3api list-objects-v2' which gives full control over pagination.

title: Copy files to/from S3
description: Copy files between the local filesystem and S3, or between two S3 locations — handles single files or entire directory trees with --recursive.

breakdown.meaning: Copy a file or directory to/from S3 or between S3 locations
Local source directory
S3 destination with prefix (folder)
Copy all files in the directory, preserving structure

flags.description: Copy an entire directory tree
Exclude files matching a glob pattern
Include files matching a pattern (after exclude)
Preview what would be copied without transferring anything
Enable server-side encryption at rest
Set Cache-Control header for static asset caching

output:
copy: ./build/index.html to s3://my-bucket/releases/v1.0/index.html
copy: ./build/main.js to s3://my-bucket/releases/v1.0/main.js
copy: ./build/styles.css to s3://my-bucket/releases/v1.0/styles.css
tip: Use --dryrun to preview operations before executing, especially for destructive or large transfers. Add --cache-control 'max-age=31536000,immutable' for versioned static assets and --sse AES256 for encryption at rest.

title: Sync directory to S3
description: Synchronise a local directory to S3 by uploading new or changed files and optionally deleting objects that no longer exist locally — the standard pattern for static site deployment.

breakdown.meaning: Sync files between local and S3 — only transfers what has changed
Local source directory to sync from
Destination S3 bucket or prefix
Remove S3 objects that no longer exist in the local source

flags.description: Delete objects in destination that are absent from source
Preview the sync without making any changes
Skip files matching a glob (e.g. --exclude '*.DS_Store')
Set object ACL — use for publicly accessible static sites
Set Cache-Control header on uploaded objects

example: aws s3 sync s3://source-bucket s3://dest-bucket --source-region us-east-1 --region eu-west-1
output:
upload: dist/index.html to s3://my-bucket/index.html
upload: dist/app.js to s3://my-bucket/app.js
delete: s3://my-bucket/old-chunk-abc123.js
tip: Always run --dryrun first when using --delete — it can permanently remove S3 objects if the source path is wrong. Use --exclude '*.map' to skip source maps and --cache-control 'no-cache' for HTML files alongside 'max-age=31536000' for hashed assets.

title: List EC2 instances
description: List EC2 instances with their IDs, state, type, and IP addresses — filter by state, tags, or attributes to narrow the results.

breakdown.meaning: Retrieve instance metadata for all or specified EC2 instances
Only return instances in the 'running' state
Render results as an ASCII table instead of JSON

flags.description: Filter by state, tag, VPC, instance type, and many other attributes
Query specific instance IDs directly
JMESPath expression to extract specific fields from nested JSON
Output format — use text for shell scripting, table for human review

tip: Use --query with JMESPath to flatten the nested Reservations[*].Instances[*] structure and extract only the fields you need. Filter by tag with 'Name=tag:Name,Values=my-server' to find instances by their Name tag.

title: Start EC2 instance
description: Start one or more stopped EC2 instances by ID — instances must be in the 'stopped' state, not 'terminated' or 'pending'.

breakdown.meaning: Send a start request to one or more stopped instances
One or more instance IDs — space-separated for multiple

flags.description: One or more instance IDs to start
Verify permissions without actually starting the instance

example: aws ec2 start-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0 && aws ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0
tip: Chain with 'aws ec2 wait instance-running --instance-ids i-xxx' to block the script until the instance is fully running before the next step. Use SSM Session Manager or EC2 Instance Connect to connect without opening port 22.

title: Stop EC2 instance
description: Gracefully stop one or more running EC2 instances — compute billing stops, but attached EBS volumes continue to accrue storage charges.

breakdown.meaning: Send a stop request to one or more running instances
One or more instance IDs to stop

flags.description: One or more instance IDs to stop
Hibernate instead of stop — saves RAM contents to EBS for faster resume
Force stop without waiting for graceful OS shutdown

example: aws ec2 stop-instances --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0 && aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0
tip: Use 'aws ec2 wait instance-stopped' to block until fully stopped before taking a snapshot or detaching volumes. Use --hibernate to preserve the instance's memory state for faster restarts on supported instance types.

title: Configure kubectl for EKS
description: Add or update a kubectl context for an EKS cluster in ~/.kube/config, enabling immediate kubectl access authenticated via AWS credentials.

breakdown.meaning: Merge an EKS cluster context into the local kubeconfig file
Name of the EKS cluster to configure access for
AWS region where the cluster is deployed

flags.description: EKS cluster name
AWS region of the cluster
Set a short context name instead of the full cluster ARN
Use a specific AWS CLI profile for authentication
Write to a specific kubeconfig file instead of ~/.kube/config

example: aws eks update-kubeconfig --name prod-cluster --region us-east-1 --alias prod --profile prod
tip: Use --alias to give the context a short name (e.g. prod) instead of the full ARN — makes switching with 'kubectl config use-context prod' much faster. Use --profile to bind the context to a specific AWS profile with the right IAM permissions.

command: aws ecr get-login-password --region us-east-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
title: Authenticate to ECR
description: Authenticate Docker to push and pull images from an Elastic Container Registry — the token is valid for 12 hours and must be refreshed in CI pipelines.

breakdown.meaning: Generate a temporary ECR authentication token
Region of the ECR registry
Pipe the token directly into Docker login — avoids the password appearing in shell history
ECR registry URL: account-id.dkr.ecr.region.amazonaws.com

flags.description: AWS region of the ECR registry
AWS profile to use for authentication

example: aws ecr get-login-password --region eu-west-1 | docker login --username AWS --password-stdin 123456789012.dkr.ecr.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com
tip: Never use the deprecated 'aws ecr get-login' (eval-based) approach. ECR tokens expire after 12 hours — refresh in CI before every push. In ECS and CodeBuild, the execution role automatically authenticates to ECR without this step.

title: Get IAM user details
description: Retrieve details about the current IAM user including the ARN, path, creation date, and password last used — useful for confirming identity and auditing access.

breakdown.meaning: IAM (Identity and Access Management) service commands
Return details for the current user, or a named user with --user-name

flags.description: Get details for a specific user instead of the calling user
List all IAM users in the account
Show managed policies attached to a user

tip: For roles rather than users (e.g. when running in EC2 or Lambda), use 'aws sts get-caller-identity' instead — get-user fails for role-based sessions. Use 'aws iam list-attached-user-policies' to audit what a user can do.

title: Invoke Lambda function
description: Synchronously invoke a Lambda function with a JSON payload and write the response to a file — useful for testing functions and triggering serverless jobs from scripts.

breakdown.meaning: Call a Lambda function and wait for the response
Function name, ARN, or partial ARN of the Lambda to invoke
JSON event payload passed to the function handler
Output file where the function's response body is written

flags.description: Lambda function name or ARN
JSON event object passed to the handler
Async invocation — returns immediately without waiting for the response
Invoke a specific version or alias
Include the last 4KB of CloudWatch logs in the response (base64-encoded)

example: aws lambda invoke --function-name my-function --payload '{"action":"process"}' --log-type Tail out.json && cat out.json
tip: Use --invocation-type Event for fire-and-forget async invocations that do not need a response. Use --log-type Tail to get the last 4KB of CloudWatch logs inline in the CLI response — decode them with: echo LOG_BASE64 | base64 -d.

title: Tail CloudWatch logs
description: Stream real-time log output from a CloudWatch log group — equivalent to tail -f for AWS services including Lambda, ECS, API Gateway, and EC2.

breakdown.meaning: Stream recent and live log events from a CloudWatch log group
Log group name — Lambda groups follow the /aws/lambda/function-name pattern
Stay connected and print new log events as they arrive (like tail -f)

flags.description: Keep streaming new events rather than exiting after current logs
Start from this far back (e.g. 30m, 1h, 2d)
Log line format — short strips request IDs for cleaner output
CloudWatch filter pattern to show only matching log events

output:
2025-03-15T10:30:45 START RequestId: abc-123-def
2025-03-15T10:30:45 Processing 47 records...
2025-03-15T10:30:46 END RequestId: abc-123-def
2025-03-15T10:30:46 REPORT Duration: 234.56ms  Billed: 235ms  Memory: 256MB  Max: 87MB
tip: Use --since 30m to avoid replaying hours of history on startup. Use --filter-pattern 'ERROR' to show only error lines — this is a server-side filter that reduces output volume. Use --format short to strip request ID noise from Lambda logs.

title: Read SSM parameter
description: Retrieve a value from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store — use --with-decryption for SecureString parameters encrypted with KMS.

breakdown.meaning: Retrieve a single parameter from SSM Parameter Store
Full parameter path — hierarchical paths with / are recommended for organisation
Decrypt SecureString parameters using KMS — required to read the plaintext value

flags.description: Full parameter name or path
Decrypt SecureString values — requires kms:Decrypt permission
Extract just the value using JMESPath
Retrieve all parameters under a path prefix

tip: Use --query 'Parameter.Value' --output text to get just the value for injection into scripts or environment variables. Use 'get-parameters-by-path --path /app/prod/ --recursive --with-decryption' to bulk-fetch all params for an environment at once.

title: Read Secrets Manager secret
description: Retrieve a secret from AWS Secrets Manager — returns the secret string or binary along with ARN, version metadata, and rotation status.

breakdown.meaning: AWS Secrets Manager service — stores and rotates credentials, API keys, and certificates
Retrieve the current value of a secret
Secret name or ARN — hierarchical names like prod/app/db are recommended

flags.description: Secret name or full ARN
Retrieve a specific version of the secret
Extract just the secret value field

example: aws secretsmanager get-secret-value --secret-id prod/myapp/database --query 'SecretString' --output text | jq '.password'
tip: Pipe --query 'SecretString' --output text into jq to extract individual fields from JSON secrets. In Lambda and ECS, use the SDK to fetch secrets directly at runtime — the execution role handles auth without any CLI config.

title: Check CloudFormation stack
description: Describe a CloudFormation stack to check its deployment status, outputs, and parameters — useful for monitoring deployments and extracting resource values.

breakdown.meaning: Get metadata for one or all CloudFormation stacks
The stack to inspect — omit to list all stacks
Extract the status field: CREATE_COMPLETE, UPDATE_FAILED, ROLLBACK_IN_PROGRESS, etc.
Print plain text — removes JSON wrapper, suitable for scripting

flags.description: Target a specific stack by name or ID
Extract stack outputs (exported resource IDs, URLs, ARNs)
See per-resource events — essential for diagnosing stuck or failed stacks
Block until stack update finishes — use in deployment scripts

tip: Use 'aws cloudformation wait stack-update-complete --stack-name my-stack' to block a deployment script until the update finishes. When a stack gets stuck, 'describe-stack-events' with a filter on UPDATE_FAILED is the fastest path to the error message.

title: List RDS instances
description: List all RDS database instances in the region with their identifiers, status, endpoint hostnames, and instance types.

breakdown.meaning: Retrieve metadata for all or specified RDS instances in the current region
JMESPath expression selecting specific fields from the nested response
Render as an ASCII table for human-readable output

flags.description: Query a specific RDS instance by ID
Filter results by instance attributes
Extract the hostname of the first instance for connection strings

tip: Use --db-instance-identifier to query a single instance. Extract the connection string with '--query DBInstances[0].Endpoint.Address --output text' — pipe into a psql or mysql connection command for automation.
